sections.title: Soup, main course, dessert
sections.content: A restaurant meal comes in courses: *leves* (soup), *saláta* (salad), *főétel* (main course) and *desszert* (dessert). A *köret* is a side dish. When you order a course it is the object, so it takes *-t*, as in *Kérek egy levest.* You already know *hús* (meat) and *hal* (fish), and they take *-t* too.

sections.title: Three patterns
sections.content: Some words just add *-t* (*leves → levest*, *hús → húst*, *főétel → főételt*). A final *-a* lengthens (*saláta → salátát*). Some words add a linking vowel (*desszert → desszertet*, *köret → köretet*, *hal → halat*). Learn each as a pair.

items.spanish: Egy salátát és egy főételt kérek.
items.english: I would like a salad and a main course.
Károly asks for meat and a side dish.
I would like a dessert too.

sections.content: The *-t* is always there when you order: *Kérek egy levest*, never *Kérek egy leves*. Ordering is doing something to the dish, so the dish is the object.
